subject: Private runtime egress binding for Acme Health - IPs & firewall steps

Subject: Private runtime egress — list of requirements and questions

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Acme's network team reviewed the Private runtime design and we have a few outstanding items before we can sign off:

- We need a definitive list of source IPs (CIDR blocks) that Redwood will use when the private connector is active so our perimeter firewall can be configured.
- Can you confirm whether outbound traffic will originate from a static NAT IP per customer, or from a pool shared across customers in the same region?
- Do you support an outbound proxy/bastion model (customer-managed), or does Redwood require traffic to flow through Redwood-managed egress proxies? Details on MTLS and client certs appreciated.
- Any DNS split-horizon or SNI considerations we need to include in our inspection policies?

I've attached our internal egress checklist and the SOW draft (acme_egress_requirements.pdf). Please reply with the required artifacts and at least a week-long window for our firewall change.

Sara Patel
Senior IT Operations Manager
Acme Health

From: markus_klein@redwood.com

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private runtime egress — list of requirements and questions

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Answered inline below and attached the IP set we recommend for this deployment.

- Source IPs: Redwood can originate outbound connections from a small set of stable egress IP blocks per region. For your region (us-west-2) the proposed blocks are: 3.12.45.128/26, 3.12.46.0/26, 3.12.47.0/26. See redwood-egress-ips-v2.csv attached. These are announced/owned by Redwood and we can provide ROA/RPKI proof if needed.

- Static per-customer NAT: We offer two modes: 1) Dedicated egress IP per customer (recommended for HIPAA/regulated tenants) — requires an extra reserved NAT allocation; 2) Shared regional pool with per-tenant source port obfuscation. For Acme we recommend Dedicated egress IPs if you'd like strict allowlisting.

- Proxy model: Redwood supports both customer-managed outbound proxies and Redwood-managed egress proxies. For private/on-prem connect we typically recommend customer-managed proxy in the DMZ that routes to Redwood control plane over mTLS. If you prefer Redwood-managed egress, we provide client certs and mutual TLS for control-plane-to-onprem callbacks. I'll loop Kimberly for the specific tunnel and TLS cert guidance.

- DNS / SNI: If you intend to do TLS inspection, avoid terminating TLS for traffic to Redwood api endpoints — use SNI-based routing and allowlist the destination FQDNs (api.redwood-inference.com and regional variants). For split-horizon DNS, ensure your private DNS resolves the internal connector to the customer gateway; otherwise we'll observe differences in egress FQDNs.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm you want Dedicated egress IPs so we can provision the NATs and update the SOW; 2) We'll provide a final artifact pack (IP CSV, CIDR ROA statements, TLS fingerprinting notes) and proposed change window.

Attachments: redwood-egress-ips-v2.csv, egress-proxy-design.pdf

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private runtime egress — technical notes and checklist

Markus / Sara — adding a few technical constraints and an ops checklist from the infra side.

Key notes:
- Hairpinning / Return Paths: If you provision Dedicated egress IPs, ensure your firewall allows return flows to the allocated NATs. If Acme uses a stateful perimeter firewall with asymmetric routing, we recommend configuring a static route back to Redwood's NAT IPs or using an external NAT gateway to solve return path issues.

- TLS inspection: For compliance, if Acme must inspect outbound TLS, require the firewall to skip deep TLS interception for traffic to Redwood's API FQDNs. Otherwise client cert mTLS will fail. Use SNI allowlist as Mark said.

- MTLS and client certs: For the control plane handshake we will provide a CA chain and leaf certs per installation. If you operate an outbound proxy that performs TLS interception, please place mTLS endpoints on an allowlist bypass.

- Ports and FQDNs: Allow outbound to 443 over the destination FQDNs below. If you must allow by IP, use the CSV we attached but be aware we may add ephemeral ICMP/UDP for health checks in future updates.

Ops checklist (for firewall change window):
1) Apply temporary ACLs for redwood egress CIDRs (test window 1 week).
2) Validate reverse path reachability from your DMZ/NAT.
3) Confirm proxy rules bypass for mTLS endpoints and update inspection exceptions.
4) Coordinate rollback steps (we can provide script to revoke NATs if needed).

Attachment: egress-proxy-design.pdf
